views.reconstructed_statement: The proposition is a conjunction of two universally quantified claims about maps on PrimitiveBasis N = (Fin N → Fin 2). First, for every natural N and every c₀,c₁,t ∈ Fin N satisfying c₀ ≠ t and c₁ ≠ t, the action ccxBasisAction c₀ c₁ t is involutive: for every binary basis string b, applying this action twice returns exactly b. The action flips only the t coordinate when both the original c₀ and c₁ bits are 1, and otherwise leaves b unchanged. No inequality between c₀ and c₁ is assumed, so coincident control indices are included. Second, for every natural N and every c,t ∈ Fin N with c ≠ t, the function ccxBasisAction c c t equals the function cxBasisAction c t, i.e. the coincident-control action agrees on every binary string with the single-control action that leaves the input unchanged when bit c is 0 and flips bit t otherwise. The claims quantify over all natural N; absent wire choices (N = 0) or impossible distinct-control/target conditions are vacuous. No assertion is made here for a control that is the target.

Fix N = 2 and the action F = ccxBasisAction (0 : Fin 2) (1 : Fin 2) (0 : Fin 2), so its first control is also its target. Let u : Fin 2 → Fin 2 be the constant-one function (u(0)=u(1)=1), and v : Fin 2 → Fin 2 be the function equal to 0 at coordinate 0 and 1 otherwise (v(0)=0, v(1)=1). The proposition asserts all of the following conjunctively: F(u)=v, F(v)=v, u≠v, ¬Function.Injective F, and ¬Function.Involutive F. Thus these particular distinct two-wire binary strings have the same image, and the action is not injective; there also exists an input that is not restored by applying F twice (in particular u), so F is not an involution. All indices and values in this statement are the specified elements of Fin 2; this is a fixed counterexample, not a universal failure claim for arbitrary overlapping controls or dimensions.
